newsitem.title: USA: Tight supply firms U.S. Group Three unleaded.
newsitem.headline: Tight supply firms U.S. Group Three unleaded.

text.p: U.S. spot unleaded prices in Group Three markets firmed on Monday after maintenance on the Explorer Pipeline last month created a shortage in supply not expected to be made up until the month's end, traders said.
The Chicago markets, meanwhile, were talked largely steady in what was a relatively quiet day all around.

Group Three unleaded differentials firmed about a penny since Friday, pegged at between 2.75/3.00 cents a gallon over June NYMEX unleaded. Traders said prompt Group unleaded changed hands at 3.00 cents over as well as a 2.50 cent deal over June NYMEX.
"Unleaded is a little firmer because we are short on supply," said a Group Three trader.
The market has been short since the Houston-to-Chicago Explorer system went down for maintenance last month.
Although the Williams pipeline has been picking up some of the slack, traders said there is only 18 days worth of supply.
Explorer has said liftings on jet fuel, gasoline and distillates should return to normal by the end of May.
Prompt Group Three premium gasoline "regrade" diffs were also up about a half cent from Friday to 3.25/3.50 cent over Group Three regular unleaded.
Group Three low sulphur diesel for May deliveries was talked between 5.50/6.00 cents a gallon over June NYMEX heating oil, with Chicago low sulphur pegged at 3.25/3.50 cents over the June print.
